changes.now: Plan, then Activity lists every quick update and save from the last 30 days, newest first: who, when, and what changed. You can show one person's. It's a record kept in the plan file, so it's a guide, not proof.

changes.title: Mine
changes.now: Next to Everyone and Jira only, Mine shows Jira's work plus what you added. A line says how many items added by others are hidden, and how many have no recorded author.

changes.title: A note's author stays its author
changes.before: Anyone could change who wrote a note.
changes.now: The author is shown, not editable. Editing someone else's note reminds you they're their words.

changes.title: Put back what an older copy dropped
changes.now: If a copy of Sightline older than 1.19 saves over the plan and drops who added what or the activity log, the page offers Put them back.

changes.title: Everyone needs this version to edit
changes.now: Plans with who added what open read-only in Sightline 1.19, and older copies drop it when they save, so update every copy.

headline: groundwork: safer saves across versions, bigger plans

changes.title: Plans saved by a newer Sightline open read-only
changes.before: An older copy of Sightline could open a plan saved by a newer one and, on saving, silently drop what it didn't understand.
changes.now: A copy that finds parts it doesn't know opens the plan read-only and says why, so nothing is lost. Update the copy to edit.

changes.title: You'll know when an older copy saved over the plan
changes.now: Each save records which Sightline wrote it. If a copy from before this version saves over the plan, the page says so, so you can ask everyone to update.

changes.title: Bigger plans open
changes.before: Plans over 2 MB couldn't be opened.
changes.now: Plans up to 5 MB open. Saving still keeps a plan under 2 MB, so every copy of Sightline can open it.

changes.title: Undo uses less memory on big plans
changes.now: Undo keeps as many steps as fit in a fixed amount of memory, newest first, instead of 200 whole copies of the plan.

changes.title: Groundwork for a shared database
changes.now: Behind the scenes, reading, saving, merging and drafts now go through one place, so the plan can later live in a database instead of a file without changing how you work.

headline: Jira's titles and assignees, always current; drag milestones and gates anywhere

changes.title: Titles and assignees always match Jira
changes.before: When you put an epic on the board or added an issue, Sightline copied its title and assignee into the plan. After a rename or reassignment in Jira, the plan showed the old ones.
changes.now: A Jira item's title and assignee are read from the latest sync everywhere: the timeline, cards, the hover, Find and Today. The card shows them read-only, marked as from Jira. Without the Jira files, the title from when it was added shows, marked as not current.

changes.title: The plan's own name on the chart, and its own lead
changes.now: A Jira item can carry a short name on the chart and a lead, both the plan's. Owners that were only a copy of the assignee aren't shown as a lead. The people filter and people rows count Jira's assignee.
changes.where: The card of a Jira item.

changes.title: Review titles that differ from Jira
changes.now: Plan, then Epics lists items whose stored title differs from Jira's. For each one, keep the plan's name on the chart, or let it follow Jira. Nothing is rewritten on its own.

changes.title: Jira's sprint names can't be edited here
changes.now: Once the plan follows Jira's sprints, their names and goals are read-only in Sightline. The plan's own timeboxes stay editable.

changes.title: Drag milestones, gates and notes
changes.before: In the Days view, milestones, gates and notes could only be opened, not moved. Gates couldn't be dragged in Weeks either.
changes.now: Drag them along their row to another day. A click still opens them. A milestone that follows initiatives says so instead of moving.

changes.title: Unsaved changes you can see, and count
changes.before: After undoing everything, the strip still said unsaved changes.
changes.now: The strip counts what's changed since the last save ("3 unsaved changes"), and clicking the count lists each change. Undoing all the way back, or putting something back as it was, reads as saved.

changes.title: Nothing added around a Jira item is lost if Jira drops it
changes.now: If a sync stops returning an issue, everything the team added around it stays and reattaches when the issue comes back. This is now in the product charter.

headline: see what comes from Jira, and what was added here

changes.title: From Jira and Added here look different
changes.before: An initiative or task linked to Jira looked like any other, so you couldn't tell what followed Jira from what the team had added.
changes.now: What comes from Jira is outlined in its workstream's color, with its Jira key. What was added here stays filled. This holds in Weeks, Days and the people rows, for initiatives, tasks and stories. The key explains both.

changes.title: Show only what comes from Jira
changes.now: Everyone / Jira only, next to the other view controls, shows the official Jira work on its own. A line under the controls says how many items added here are hidden, with Show everyone. Each plan remembers its own choice in your browser, and a saved view can keep it.

changes.title: Progress says what it counts
changes.before: Bars showed a bare percentage (weighted by task length) or an unlabeled 3/4.
changes.now: Bars show 5/9 stories for Jira work and 2/5 tasks (or items) for work added here, and the fill matches the count. The weighted percentage is in the hover and the card, marked as by task-days.

changes.title: Jira's sprints and the plan's own timeboxes
changes.now: When the plan follows Jira's sprints, a timebox the plan added (after Jira's last sprint, say) shows in italics. Hovering a Jira sprint shows Jira's exact dates.

changes.title: Parked initiatives are counted
changes.before: Parked initiatives just disappeared from the timeline.
changes.now: A line says how many are parked, with a link to Plan, then Epics.

headline: undo quick updates, and groups that stay open

changes.title: Undo works on Park, Put on the board, and switching stories
changes.before: These save straight to the shared file, so Undo had nothing to undo unless you were in an editing session.
changes.now: Undo (and Ctrl+Z) reverses the last quick update in the shared file, key by key, so a teammate's newer changes stay. Redo puts it back, and a toast after each decision offers Undo. The Undo button names what it will undo.
changes.where: Plan, then Epics; the initiative and story cards.

changes.title: Epics groups stay the way you left them
changes.before: Clicking Back on (or anything that redraws the list) snapped the Parked and Finished groups shut.
changes.now: Each group remembers being opened or closed.

changes.title: Sprints after Jira's last one continue its numbering
changes.before: When the plan kept its own sprints after Jira's last one, they kept the plan's old numbers, so Sprint 45 could be followed by Sprint 48. The weeks before Jira's first sprint were called a gap between sprints.
changes.now: Numbered sprints continue from Jira (Sprint 46, 47…), and a named one like Hardening keeps its name. The weeks before Jira's first sprint say so, with a note on how to start the plan there instead.
changes.where: Settings, then Jira, then Sprints from Jira.

headline: finished epics stay out of your way

changes.title: Sightline knows when an epic is finished
changes.before: Old epics came in with the live ones, because teams often leave an epic open long after its stories are done, so sorting meant opening each one to check.
changes.now: The sync counts the stories under every epic your searches find. An epic whose stories are all done or abandoned goes into a closed Finished in Jira group: it isn't in Unsorted, isn't counted as to sort, and isn't touched by Park all. A new epic with no stories yet stays in Unsorted. Each row says how many stories are open.

changes.title: Park finished epics in one click
changes.now: When epics on the board are finished in Jira, Epics says how many and offers Park N finished. It keeps their initiatives and notes, and takes them off the timeline.

changes.title: Counts for every epic a search finds
changes.now: Epics on the board are counted first (with their stories listed), then the other epics your searches found (counted only), all within the same 5,000-story limit. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again.

headline: sorting that respects your picks, and a lighter page

changes.title: Parking the rest leaves your picks alone
changes.before: Park the other N also parked the epics you had just ticked.
changes.now: With epics picked, the button parks only the ones you haven't picked, and says how many.

changes.title: Stories are easy to find from Weeks
changes.before: Jira stories show only in the Days view, and nothing in Weeks said so.
changes.now: An initiative's card has See N on the timeline, which opens Days at its stories, and its hover card says how many are in sprints. Find says when a story is switched off, has no sprint yet, or is outside this plan.

changes.title: Shorter, clearer words
changes.now: Stories switch off and on with Switch off and Switch on. The health warnings are one line each, and Settings says Reconnect when the folder needs your OK.
changes.where: Initiative and story cards, Epics, Settings.

changes.title: Less work while you wait
changes.before: The page reread and redrew everything every minute, even when Jira hadn't changed, which could disturb what you were typing.
changes.now: It redraws only when a Jira file changes. Epic counts and ownership are worked out once per draw instead of several times.

headline: see whether Jira is keeping up

changes.title: Sync health
changes.before: The page said when the Jira files were written, but not whether that was on time, so a stopped sync looked the same as a quiet week.
changes.now: Epics and Settings show when Jira last synced, whether by watch (and how often) or by hand, and from which server and board, with a green, amber or red dot. When a watch is more than twice its interval late, the page says so and what to check: that the computer running it is on and signed in. It updates every minute while the page is open.

changes.title: Flags Jira files made for another plan
changes.now: If you copied or renamed the plan's folder, the page says the Jira files were made for the other plan and how to set up the sync for this one.

changes.title: The sync says how it runs
changes.now: status.json records whether watch or a one-off sync wrote it, its interval, and the plan's file name. It records no computer or user names. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again.

headline: stories: counts that agree, and switches that stick

changes.title: Reconnect Jira in one click
changes.before: After the browser restarted, Epics said to connect the folder in Settings, so getting Jira back took a trip through Plan, Settings and the folder picker.
changes.now: Epics shows a Reconnect button for your folder, and one click brings everything back. When you open the page, the status line says Jira is paused until you reconnect. Plan opens on Epics for plans that use Jira. Your browser may offer to allow the folder on every visit, so you won't be asked again.

changes.title: Two people switching stories off at once both count
changes.before: When two quick updates clashed, the retry could keep only one person's switched-off story. The same was true for parked epics and the status map.
changes.now: A retried update adds and removes just its own keys, so everyone's changes survive.
changes.where: Off for now, Park, and the status map.

changes.title: A date filter shows stories in that range
changes.before: An initiative planned outside the dates was hidden, even when one of its Jira stories fell inside them.
changes.now: The initiative shows with its matching stories, and Find clears a filter that would hide the story it goes to.

changes.title: Every count agrees
changes.before: An epic's row in the initiative's card counted every story while the total above it didn't. A story linked to two epics could count twice. With a very large epic, counts could go below zero.
changes.now: The same rule counts everywhere, off for now is shown on each epic, each story counts once, and no count goes below zero. Needs the updated sync script for the two-epics fix.
changes.where: The initiative's card, and Plan, then Epics.

changes.title: No silent limit on stories off
changes.before: Past 2,000 stories off for now, switching off another quietly switched the oldest back on.
changes.now: It says the limit was reached instead.

changes.title: A new epic says its stories are coming
changes.now: Until the next sync lists them, the card says the stories show after the next Jira sync, and when the last one ran.

headline: an epic's stories, inside its initiative

changes.title: Stories from Jira show inside their initiative
changes.before: An epic on the board showed only as a count of its stories.
changes.now: In the Days view, each story in a sprint shows inside its initiative: its sprint sets the dates and Jira sets the status. Stories have a dashed outline and their Jira key. Click one for its card. They're read-only, so change them in Jira. They aren't copied into the plan, and a story that's already a task in the plan shows as the task.

changes.title: Switch a story off for now
changes.now: Every initiative with epics lists its stories: in a sprint, not scheduled here, off for now, and abandoned in Jira. Off for now hides a story from the timeline and from progress, without changing Jira. Anyone can do it without Start editing, and two people's changes both count. Everyone should use this version, because older copies drop the list when they save.
changes.where: The initiative's card, or the story's card.

changes.title: Progress counts what's switched on
changes.before: Progress counted every story under the epic.
changes.now: Only stories that are switched on count. Plan, then Epics shows how many are off for now. Switching off every story no longer marks the initiative abandoned.

changes.title: Find and filters include stories
changes.now: Find lists each story by its key, name and assignee. Status and people filters show the stories that match.

changes.title: The sync lists each epic's stories
changes.now: For epics on the board, the status file lists up to 3,000 stories with their sprint and status. Parked epics are counted but not listed. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again.

headline: epic decisions that stick, and a sync that keeps going

changes.title: Park means parked
changes.before: Parking an epic that an initiative was made from by its key, or one tied to a hand-made initiative, could leave it on the board while the list said Parked.
changes.now: Each epic belongs to one initiative, however it was linked. Park and Park all switch it off everywhere, and On… won't make a second initiative for an epic that's already on the board.

changes.title: Messages say what really happened
changes.before: Putting epics on the board or parking them always said it worked, even when the save didn't happen, and cleared your picks.
changes.now: If it didn't save, your picks stay. In an editing session it says the change waits for Save. Back on explains when the epic's initiative was removed.

changes.title: Scheduling leaves Jira stories in their sprint
changes.before: A dependency could push a Jira story out of its sprint, and the next redraw put it back, so the plan never settled.
changes.now: Jira's sprint dates stay fixed when the plan schedules itself. A clash shows as a warning instead.

changes.title: Statuses with a | in their name
changes.before: A Jira status like Done | QA was misread in epic progress.
changes.now: It's counted under its real name. Needs the updated sync script.
changes.where: Epic progress and the status map.

changes.title: watch keeps going
changes.before: An unexpected error (a half-saved plan, a full disk) could stop watch for every plan, a failed sync waited the full interval to retry, and two watches could both start.
changes.now: A failure is reported for that plan only and retried after a minute, then less often. Only one watch runs on a computer, and one that loses the lock stops.

changes.title: sync --save changes only what you give it
changes.before: sync PLAN --board 8 --save replaced the saved searches and folder with nothing, and saved even if the sync then failed.
changes.now: Each option replaces just that setting, and settings are saved only after a sync works. When several searches fill the file, the later ones say they were skipped.

headline: workstreams, a Settings page, and sorting many epics at once

changes.title: Lanes are now called workstreams
changes.before: The rows were called lanes, which describes the drawing rather than what they mean.
changes.now: A workstream is an area or priority the team's work belongs to, lasting quarters. Initiatives sit inside it, and stories inside those. Only the name changed: plans and older copies keep working.
changes.where: Everywhere lanes used to be named.

changes.title: Pick several epics, then decide once
changes.before: Each epic took its own round trip to the shared file, which was slow.
changes.now: Tick epics (or Pick all), choose a workstream, and put them all on the board, or park them all, in one save.

changes.title: Make a workstream while you sort
changes.now: + New workstream is in the picked bar and in each epic's On… menu.

changes.title: One Settings page
changes.now: The plan's dates and sprints, and everything about connecting Jira (the folder, the status map, sprints from the board, your searches), are on one page.
changes.where: The gear button at the top, or File, then Jira status.

changes.title: Epics live under Plan
changes.before: Epics had a tab of their own.
changes.now: Sorting epics is planning work, so it's a list under Plan, next to Milestones and Risks. The Plan tab's badge counts epics waiting to be sorted.

headline: tidier meeting attendees

changes.title: Adding a group tidies the People list
changes.before: Adding a group to a meeting left its members listed one by one as well.
changes.now: People the group already brings are taken off the People list; nobody is dropped from the meeting. A meeting that already lists group members one by one says so, with a one-click fix.
changes.where: A meeting's details panel, under Groups and People.

changes.title: Names in lists no longer run together
changes.before: Attendee names in the meetings and groups tables had no space between them.
changes.now: Each name has room, and long lists wrap.

headline: a Jira tab for putting epics on the board

changes.title: A Jira tab: epics on the board, parked, or not sorted yet
changes.before: Jira issues were added one batch at a time from a pop-up.
changes.now: Every epic your searches find is in one of three groups. Switch one on as a new initiative in a lane, or add it to an initiative you already have (the closest names are suggested). Park the ones that don't matter right now; switch any back on later. The tab's badge counts epics nobody has sorted.
changes.where: The Jira tab, next to Plan (or press 5).

changes.title: Sort your epics once
changes.now: The first time, switch on the epics this plan tracks and park the rest in one go. After that, only new epics wait to be sorted.

changes.title: Parking never deletes
changes.now: Parking an epic that has its own initiative hides the initiative, with its notes and links kept, until you switch it back on. An initiative that holds other work just lets go of the epic.
changes.where: The Jira tab, Park and Back on.

changes.title: Anyone can sort epics
changes.before: Adding issues from Jira needed Start editing.
changes.now: Switching epics on and off are quick updates: no Start editing, and two people's choices both count.

changes.title: Epic initiatives follow their stories' sprints
changes.before: It suggested a stretch you had to click.
changes.now: An initiative made of epics covers its stories' sprints on its own, and can't be dragged away from them.

changes.title: Setup moved to the Jira tab
changes.now: The folder, status map, sprints and all search results are in the tab's Setup section.

headline: several Jira searches per plan

changes.title: Keep several Jira searches side by side
changes.before: A plan could have one Jira search, so seeing epics and this sprint's stories meant switching searches.
changes.now: Give the sync as many named searches as you need, like Epics, This sprint and No epic. The Jira window has a button for each, with how many are new, and Today says how many are new in each.

headline: Jira keeps itself in sync, and every project carries its own jira folder

changes.title: A plan's Jira files live in a jira folder next to it
changes.before: The sync wrote jira-status.json and jira-issues.json loose next to the plan, and each had to be connected separately.
changes.now: The sync writes the plan's Jira files into a jira folder next to the plan, so the folder can be copied for another project. Connect that folder once and Sightline reads everything in it, every minute.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, then Connect the Jira folder.

changes.title: Clearer when nothing is linked yet
changes.before: The Jira window said Jira and the plan agree on every linked item even when nothing was linked.
changes.now: It says nothing in the plan is linked to Jira yet.

changes.title: Set it up once; it keeps itself in sync
changes.before: Every sync meant running a long command by hand, and adding epics meant running it twice.
changes.now: sync --save remembers a plan's board and search on your computer. install starts watch when you sign in: every saved plan syncs on its schedule, and again shortly after anyone saves the plan.

changes.title: More than one Jira
changes.now: Set up as many Jira servers as you need (setup --jira URL). Each plan remembers which one it uses, with that server's own fields.

changes.title: Your token only runs your own copy of the sync
changes.before: The sync ran from the shared folder, so anyone who could edit that folder could change what ran with your Jira token.
changes.now: install keeps your own copy in your profile, and the sync warns when it's run from anywhere else.

headline: Sightline survives being copied, and says so when it can't start

changes.title: A copy that re-encodes the file no longer stops Sightline
changes.before: Sightline runs only its own code, checked by fingerprint. If a copy changed any character in that code, for example by saving it in another text encoding, the browser blocked all of it and the page stayed blank.
changes.now: The code is written in plain ASCII, so re-encoding the file can't change it. A checksum file comes with each copy.

changes.title: A clear message when Sightline can't start
changes.before: A blocked page was blank, with the reason only in the browser's console.
changes.now: The page says Sightline didn't start, why that usually happens, and how to check and fix the copy. Your plan file isn't affected.
changes.where: Opening a damaged copy of timeline-planner.html.

headline: Jira statuses show the way your board does, and abandoned work stops counting as done

changes.title: Abandoned work is no longer counted as done
changes.before: Jira puts abandoned issues in its Done category, so Sightline counted them as finished.
changes.now: Work closed as Won't Do, Duplicate or Cancelled is shown as Abandoned: struck through, and left out of progress and story counts. Initiatives say how many were abandoned.
changes.where: The chart, an initiative's Jira epics, and progress.

changes.title: Statuses follow your board's columns
changes.before: Sightline used Jira's own status categories, which put some statuses in the wrong place (Completed as in progress, Resolved as to do).
changes.now: Run the sync with --board and Sightline reads the board's columns: early columns are not started, middle ones are in progress (shown by the column's name, like Pending Acceptance), the last is done. Abandoned statuses in the Done column show as Abandoned.

changes.title: A status map the team shares
changes.now: The Jira window lists every status and resolution your issues use, how each shows here, and why. Change any that are wrong; the whole team sees the same, and counts update at once.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, under How Jira statuses show in Sightline.

changes.title: Parking-lot sprints don't schedule anything
changes.before: An issue parked in such a sprint was pinned to its old dates.
changes.now: A future sprint whose dates have passed (like To Be Evaluated by Leads) no longer sets an issue's dates or shapes the plan's sprints. Its issues say they're not in a scheduled sprint.
changes.where: Timeline, and Sprints from your Jira board.

headline: sprints from Jira, and Jira issues stay where Jira puts them

changes.title: The plan's sprints follow your Jira board
changes.before: Sprints in Sightline were set up by hand and could drift from Jira's.
changes.now: Run the sync with --board and the Jira window shows the plan's sprints next to Jira's. One click makes them match. Jira is the source of truth for sprint names and dates; the plan keeps its own sprints after Jira's last one.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, under Sprints from your Jira board.

changes.title: Jira issues sit in their sprint
changes.before: Items linked to a Jira story could be dragged anywhere, whatever sprint Jira had them in.
changes.now: An initiative or task linked to a Jira issue sits in that issue's sprint, and can't be dragged or resized. To move it, change its sprint in Jira. Issues not in a sprint yet can still be moved.
changes.where: Timeline, on items linked to Jira.

changes.title: Status comes from Jira
changes.before: A Jira-linked item's status was set by hand and could disagree with Jira.
changes.now: Its status follows Jira's. An initiative made of epics follows its stories. At risk and Blocked are still yours to set.

changes.title: Stretch an initiative to cover its stories' sprints
changes.now: An initiative made of epics says which sprints its stories are in, and one click stretches the bar to cover them. It never moves on its own.

changes.title: Today sends you to Jira for Jira's items
changes.now: Items whose dates and status come from Jira say Update it in Jira instead of offering Start, Done or Next week. Unblock still works.

headline: a review of the Jira work: fixes, and room for big backlogs

changes.title: Filter a long list of Jira issues
changes.before: Only the first 300 issues from a search were shown, and Select all picked all of them.
changes.now: Every issue is listed. Type to filter by key, summary, type, status, person or epic. Select all picks just the ones shown, and the buttons say how many you picked.

changes.title: An epic already linked isn't offered again
changes.before: An epic linked through an initiative's Jira epics still showed as new, and adding it made a duplicate.
changes.now: Epics linked either way count as in the plan.

changes.title: Owners come only from linked Jira users
changes.before: When Jira sent no user key, Sightline could make someone an owner because their display name matched.
changes.now: Owners are only set from a person's Jira link. Two people with the same name can't be mixed up.
changes.where: Adding issues from Jira, and Mine on Today.

changes.title: Skips and epic links from two people both survive
changes.before: If you and a teammate each skipped an issue, or each linked an epic to the same initiative, one of you could lose yours when the changes merged.
changes.now: Both are kept, and a skip or link you removed stays removed.
changes.where: When Sightline brings in a teammate's changes.

changes.title: Issues with an unknown status aren't counted as to do
changes.before: Stories whose status Jira gave no category were counted as not started.
changes.now: They're counted separately, and the initiative says how many.

changes.title: Story counts say where they come from
changes.before: The counts didn't say how old they were or whose view of Jira they reflect.
changes.now: They show when they were counted, and that only issues the person running the sync can see are included.

changes.title: The two Jira files must belong together
changes.before: A status file and an issues file from different sync runs, or different Jira servers, were used together without a word.
changes.now: Sightline says when the issues file is from an earlier sync, and refuses a pair from different Jira servers.

changes.title: No email addresses in names, either
changes.before: If someone's Jira display name was an email address, it was written into the shared files.
changes.now: The sync script uses their user name instead, or "Jira user".

headline: see how far along each initiative's Jira epics are

changes.title: Link initiatives to their Jira epics
changes.before: An initiative could link to one Jira issue, and the stories under an epic didn't count.
changes.now: Link as many epics as the work spans. The sync script counts their stories by status and adds up story points. The initiative shows how many are done, with a progress bar.
changes.where: An initiative's details panel, under Jira epics.

changes.title: Stories done, right on the bar
changes.now: An initiative with Jira epics shows stories done out of the total, like 17/45. Hover for what's in progress and the points.

changes.title: An epic's own status no longer causes false alarms
changes.before: An epic's status often stays In Progress for months, so an initiative linked to it was flagged as disagreeing with Jira even when every story was done.
changes.now: Initiatives linked to epics are compared with their stories: all done means done, any started means in progress.
changes.where: Jira and the plan disagree, in the Jira window and on Today.

changes.title: Epics are recognized even when your admins renamed the type
changes.before: Sightline only knew an issue was an epic if its type was called "Epic".
changes.now: The sync script knows epics by their Epic Name field, whatever the type is called. An epic added from your Jira search is linked as that initiative's epic, so its stories are counted.
changes.where: Run python sightline-jira-sync.py fields once to pick up the Epic Name field.

changes.title: Select all issues at once
changes.before: Picking many issues from your Jira search meant ticking each one.
changes.now: A Select all checkbox heads the list. It shows when only some are picked.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, while you're editing.

headline: Sightline learns your Jira's fields

changes.title: The sync script finds your Jira's Epic Link, Sprint and Story Points
changes.before: Every Jira server names these fields differently, so the script couldn't read them.
changes.now: Setup looks them up by type and saves them on your computer. Run fields to look again, or fields --set to choose one yourself.

changes.title: See each issue's epic, sprint and story points
changes.now: Issues from your Jira search show their epic, current sprint and points. An item's Jira line shows its sprint and points too.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, and the details panel under the Jira key.

headline: link your team to their Jira users

changes.title: Link people to their Jira users
changes.before: Sightline matched Jira assignees to people by display name only, so "Avery Smith" in Jira never matched "Avery" in the plan.
changes.now: Link each person to their Jira user once. Sightline suggests the likely match, and nothing links until you click Link. Links are saved in the plan, so the whole team shares them.
changes.where: The person's panel, or People, then Jira users.

changes.title: See everyone assigned in Jira
changes.now: People lists everyone the Jira files have work assigned to, how many issues each has, and who isn't linked yet. Link them to someone on the team, or add them to the team.
changes.where: People, then Jira users. It appears once a Jira file is connected.

changes.title: Issues from Jira get the right owner
changes.before: Adding an issue from Jira set the owner only when the display name matched exactly.
changes.now: A linked assignee becomes the owner even when their Jira name is different. An assignee who isn't linked is never guessed from their name.
changes.where: File, then Jira status, then Add picked.

changes.title: Mine includes what Jira assigns to you
changes.now: Once you're linked, Today's Mine view includes plan items whose Jira issue is assigned to you, even if you're not an owner in the plan.

changes.title: Spot work Jira assigns to someone else
changes.now: An item's Jira line says "not an owner here" when Jira's assignee isn't one of its owners.
changes.where: The details panel, under the Jira key.

changes.title: No email addresses in the Jira files
changes.now: The sync script writes each assignee's Jira key and user name, never their email. If your Jira uses email addresses as user names, the script writes a one-way code instead, which still links but can't be turned back into the address.

headline: bring in Jira issues from a filter

changes.title: Bring in issues from a Jira filter
changes.before: Sightline could only show the Jira status of items that were already in the plan.
changes.now: Give the sync script a saved filter or a search, and it writes what it finds to its own file, jira-issues.json. Connect that file in the Jira window to see the issues that aren't in the plan yet, then add them as initiatives in a lane or as tasks in an initiative. Each starts today, ends on its due date, and gets its owner when the assignee is on the team.
changes.where: File, then Jira status. Run the script with --filter 12345 or --jql "...", then Connect jira-issues.json.

changes.title: Skip issues that don't belong in the plan
changes.now: Skip picked issues to leave them out. Skips are saved in the plan, so the whole team sees the same list. Show them again any time.

changes.title: Today tells you when Jira has something new
changes.now: When the filter finds issues that aren't in the plan, Today says how many, with a Review button.

changes.title: The Jira window's lists are easier to read
changes.before: Items in the "Jira and the plan disagree" list were shown in small bold capitals.
changes.now: They're in normal text, like the rest of the window.

headline: more room for your plan, and Today leads with what needs you

changes.title: Today leads with what needs you
changes.before: Every section had its own card, even when it only said "Nothing here."
changes.now: Sections with work in them come first. Empty ones are named together on one line, and a clear day says so.

changes.title: The details panel no longer covers other pages
changes.before: What you opened on the Timeline stayed open over Today, People, and Plan, and hid part of the page.
changes.now: Picking another tab closes it. When you open something on Today, People, or Plan, the page moves over to make room.
changes.where: The details panel on the right.

changes.title: Gates on the same day share one chip
changes.before: Gates needed on the same day stacked on top of each other, so the Gates row grew tall.
changes.now: They share one chip, like "Oct 16 Admin consent +1". Click it to pick the gate you want.

changes.title: The key folds away
changes.before: The key was always open at the bottom of the chart, two lines deep.
changes.now: It folds behind a Key button, and remembers if you leave it open. The milestone that waits on a gate is now "Gated milestone", so no two entries share a name.
changes.where: Key, at the bottom of the Timeline.

changes.title: Bars show a short name when the title doesn't fit
changes.before: A long title on a short bar was cut off mid-word.
changes.now: If you haven't set a chart name, the bar shows the part before " · " or ":", the same one the panel suggests. Hover for the full title.

changes.title: One name for notes
changes.before: The panel said "Sticky notes", the toolbar "Notes", and a menu "Post-it notes", all for the same thing.
changes.now: They're called Notes everywhere. Updates are still separate: dated progress on an item.
changes.where: The details panel, and Notes in the toolbar.

changes.title: It's clear when your plan isn't shared
changes.before: "This browser only" was a small gray chip, easy to miss.
changes.now: It's drawn as a warning and says "Share…". Click it to save the plan as a shared plan, or open one your team already shares.
changes.where: The chip at the top of the page.

changes.title: Risks show how serious they are
changes.before: Severity was plain text, and a long risk was cut off in its box.
changes.now: High is red and medium is amber. The risk wraps onto more lines, and Enter finishes the edit.
changes.where: Plan, then Risks. Decisions wrap too.

changes.title: The line by the tabs says where you are in the sprint
changes.before: It repeated "By lane · Weeks", which the buttons on the right already show.
changes.now: It says where today falls in its sprint, like "S1 · day 4 of 10", then any filters.
changes.where: Next to the Today, Timeline, People, and Plan tabs.

changes.title: Line icons on Today and the details panel
changes.before: Today's sections and Mark blocked used emoji, which looked different from the rest of the page.
changes.now: They use Sightline's own line icons, colored by what needs attention.
changes.where: Today, and Mark blocked in the details panel.

headline: safer saving, a cleaner Process row, and release notes

changes.title: See what changed in each version
changes.before: There was no way to tell what changed between versions of Sightline.
changes.now: Every release is listed here, newest first. Search it, or filter by kind or area. A dot on What's new means there's a release you haven't seen yet.
changes.where: What's new, at the top right.

changes.title: The Process row reads at a glance
changes.before: At Weeks zoom, Code freeze showed as "C", and each Release sat on a second line under it.
changes.now: Each freeze is a band as wide as its days and each release is a pin on top of it, all on one line. The header names each kind in its color.
changes.where: Timeline, Weeks zoom, the Process row.

changes.title: Focus stays on the dropdown you just changed
changes.before: Changing a dropdown in the details panel with the keyboard moved focus off it.
changes.now: Focus stays on the dropdown, so you can keep working from the keyboard.
changes.where: The details panel on the right, for example Status.

changes.title: Sightline only runs its own code
changes.before: The page would have run any script placed inside it.
changes.now: The page runs only the two scripts it ships with. The browser blocks anything else.

changes.title: The + no longer covers what's already there
changes.before: Pointing at a process block, or next to one, could put the + on top of it.
changes.now: The + shows only in open space. If the spot is taken, it moves to the nearest open space in the row, or doesn't show.
changes.where: Point at an empty spot on any timeline row.

changes.title: Very large plans can't break the file anymore
changes.before: Saving a plan over 2 MB wrote a file Sightline couldn't open again.
changes.now: Sightline refuses the save and tells you how large the plan would be, so the file stays safe.
changes.where: Save, quick updates, and Start a new shared plan.

changes.title: Your edits are backed up when a teammate's change wins
changes.before: If you and a teammate changed the same thing, their newer change was kept and yours was dropped.
changes.now: Theirs is still kept, but your version is downloaded as a backup first.
changes.where: When Sightline brings in a teammate's changes.

changes.title: A teammate's undo is no longer reversed
changes.before: If a teammate undid your quick update a moment after you made it, Sightline could put your update back.
changes.now: A change made after seeing yours is left alone.
changes.where: Quick updates, like marking something done.

changes.title: When a save is refused, you can see why
changes.before: The reason a save was refused disappeared before you could read it.
changes.now: The reason stays in the status line.
changes.where: The status line at the bottom of the page.

changes.title: No more "null" in menus
changes.before: The word "null" could appear in the + menu, Notes, Filters, and the Jira window.
changes.now: Those menus show only what belongs there.
changes.where: + on the timeline, Notes, Filters, and Jira status.

changes.title: Sprint rules stay inside their sprint
changes.before: A rule like "5th working day" could land in the next sprint when a holiday made a sprint shorter.
changes.now: It lands on the sprint's last working day instead.
changes.where: Process blocks that repeat from a sprint rule.

changes.title: Tasks that wait on each other stay put
changes.before: If two tasks waited on each other, every edit pushed both of them later.
changes.now: They stay where they are and are listed as a dependency loop to fix.
changes.where: The review banner above the timeline.

changes.title: Your Jira token stays private
changes.before: If Jira redirected a request, the sync script could send your token to another address. On a Mac, other programs could briefly see it.
changes.now: Redirects are refused, and the token is handed over privately.

headline: the planner gets a name

changes.title: Meet Sightline
changes.now: The planner is now called Sightline: your team's work, in plain sight.
changes.where: The top left of the page and the browser tab.

changes.title: One plan file your whole team shares
changes.now: Link a plan file your team shares. One person edits at a time, anyone can make quick updates, and nothing is overwritten without a backup.

changes.title: Your plan by lane or by person
changes.now: See work by lane or by person, zoom from weeks to days, and plan around holidays and time off.

changes.title: Sprints, meetings, and team rhythms
changes.now: Set up sprints, repeating meetings, and process blocks like code freezes and releases that repeat every sprint from a rule.

changes.title: Jira status next to your plan
changes.now: Show each item's Jira status beside it. A small script fetches it, so the page never sees your token.
